points.claim: Aurora's roster change is real, but it is three months old - not a live excuse for the upset
points.detail: Verified line by line on 16 October 2026 (UTC). Aurora's current five, as published on HLTV's team page, is XANTARES, woxic, Jimpphat, kyxsan (in-game leader) and Wicadia, coached by Ashley 'ash' Battye. Three of those five - XANTARES, woxic and Wicadia - were already in the Turkish core, so the rebuild replaced two players plus the coach and the in-game leader, not the whole team. On the same page Aurora are ranked #5 in the world on Valve's Regional Standings and #6 on HLTV's own world ranking. Trade coverage dates the move: Jimpphat arrived from MOUZ and ash from GamerLegion, with kyxsan completing the lineup on 8 July 2026, while MAJ3R, soulfly and coach Fabre moved to the inactive roster. That is roughly a full ranking cycle before this event, over which Aurora climbed to #5 in the world, so 'new roster still bedding in' is not supported by the ranking evidence as a reason they lost to 9z. The dates come from trade-press reporting and are labelled as such; the lineup, the coach and both rankings are read from HLTV directly.

strategy.headline: Contrarian but not stupid: when an underdog is worth taking
strategy.summary: In a pick'em the favourite is usually the crowd's pick, so a correct underdog is what separates a leaderboard entry from the pack. The trade-off only pays when the underdog is backed by a verifiable reason and the price still leaves room. The rules below are project strategy, not verified outcomes.

rules.rule: Take the underdog when a roster change is recent and structural, not cosmetic.
rules.why: A new in-game leader, a new star and a new coach inside one split means an unproven system, new communication and a short practice window. Aurora's 2026 rebuild is the day-one example.
rules.verify: Official organisation announcements, the transfer timeline and the team's own statements, then confirm the current five on a fixture-specific source.

rules.rule: Take the underdog when the favourite is demonstrably fatigued and the market has not repriced.
rules.why: Deep runs plus travel compress preparation. A favourite whose price already fell has no contrarian value left.
rules.verify: Compare the favourite's recent tournament load and travel from results pages, then check whether the offered price still reflects the earlier reputation.

rules.rule: Prefer underdogs whose chance is roughly one in five or better, and expect to lose most of them.
rules.why: A 20-40% pick that wins is worth the same single point as a favourite but moves you past everyone who copied the crowd. Below that band the pick is a lottery ticket, not an edge.
rules.verify: Use the sourced market probability on the picks page. Where no market exists, use the labelled research tier and treat it as low confidence.

rules.rule: Never size up a contrarian pick on an identity or a number you cannot source.
rules.why: Renamed teams, academy squads and unclear aliases are exactly where a whole pick'em slips away on a wrong team.
rules.verify: The identity register in this project requires an exact opponent and UTC start before any alias is used.

rules.rule: Limit how many contrarian swings you take per slate.
rules.why: Stacking four underdogs multiplies variance instead of climbing the leaderboard.
rules.verify: Count the contrarian picks shown in the screen below; treat anything beyond one or two as exposure, not insight.

rules.rule: Weight the swing by what the fixture is worth, and count the streak you would break.
rules.why: Hotspawn awards more points for higher tiers and a bonus for consecutive correct picks, so a contrarian miss costs the fixture's points plus the streak. In the current feed a tier-S match is worth 7 points, tier-B 3 and tier-C 2: a wrong tier-C swing costs 2 points, a wrong tier-S swing costs 7 and the bonus run with it.
rules.verify: Hotspawn's official how-it-works rules page, which the day-three points above link directly, plus the offered_points and points_breakdown fields in the fixture feed; expected points are then offered_points x the published probability, which is arithmetic on a sourced line, never a new probability.

unverified: Hotspawn's scoring rules are now collected from the official rules page and from the fixture feed's offered_points field: points per correct pick, more points for higher tiers (7 / 3 / 2 for tiers S / B / C in the current feed), a bonus for consecutive correct picks, picks locking before start and a weekly leaderboard reset. What is still not verifiable from any source this project can read is the exact streak-bonus formula, so no number is claimed for it and no claim is made about how many extra points a correct underdog earns relative to a favourite beyond the tier weighting.
No calibrated historical model exists here: contrarian picks are market-implied plus sourced context, and are not a promise of profit or of a higher leaderboard position.

points.claim: Neither day-three decider has a rest asymmetry - every one of the four teams played on 15 October
points.detail: Read from HLTV's results page for the event. In Group A, Aurora beat Ninjas in Pyjamas 2-0 on 15 October and 9z lost 1-2 to Falcons on the same day. In Group B, BETBOOM beat PARIVISION 2-1 and Legacy lost 1-2 to FURIA, also on 15 October. Both deciders are therefore played by teams with identical rest, so fatigue is not a usable differentiator on day three. The only sourced freshness factor on this slate sits elsewhere: NIP flew from elimination in Malta to a quarter-final in Sweden with under 24 hours' turnaround, which is a cost on the Stake Pulse Beat III row, not on either TWC decider.

points.claim: Do not use 'new roster' as the contrarian case for 9z - use the head-to-head
points.detail: The user's hypothesis was that a recently changed or newly onboarded roster makes a team ripe for an upset. Checked against the sources, that does not hold for Aurora on 16 October: the change landed in July 2026 and Aurora now sit at #5 on Valve's standings and #6 on HLTV's ranking. The sourced case for 9z is narrower and stronger - they beat this exact opponent 2-0 two days earlier in this event (Inferno 13-11 and Nuke 13-1 on Aurora's own pick) and then took a map off Falcons, who won the group. A repeatable head-to-head result in the same tournament is a reason; a roster move the rankings have already absorbed is not.

points.claim: Both 16 October deciders are tier-S fixtures worth 7 points each in the official feed: fixtures 1080205 and 1081775 carry offered_points 7 with a points_breakdown of tier_multiplier 3 and game_multiplier 1.25.
points.detail: Read from the same fixture payload the collector retains in research/harvest-dedd2e34/latest.json (fixture_evidence keeps the raw row, with Hotspawn's crowd-pick percentages dropped). A swing on either decider costs or gains more than twice a tier-C fixture on the same slate, which is why the contrarian test is applied to at most one of them and why the two candidates are weighed against each other rather than added together.

points.claim: The board itself changed between two dated captures, and that is recorded in this project's own receipts rather than inferred: BetBoom vs Legacy entered the Hotspawn feed between 2026-10-15T21:33:49Z (86 rows, no BetBoom row, exactly one Legacy row) and 2026-10-16T04:22:23Z (95 rows, added_ids containing 1081775).
points.detail: Produced by run https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/MaltaProj4/actions/runs/38850237836: coverage_counts 95/95/95/95 across the API, the cs2-pickems page, the general lobby and retained rows, and inventory_changes.added_ids listing 1081775. Two scripts make this repeatable instead of anecdotal: scripts/coverage_gap_dedd2e34.py compares the board against https://www.hltv.org/events/8932/matches and writes research/harvest-dedd2e34/coverage-gap.md, and scripts/harvest_dedd2e34.py replays every published probability from its own raw inputs, so a board row can be re-derived without trusting the render. On the 16 October replay all 20 published probabilities reproduced exactly (17 exchange rows and 3 model rows, zero mismatches).

points.claim: On the Group B decider the market and our originated line agree on the winner but not on its size: the exchange prices BETBOOM at 34.5% while Valve's standings price them at 20.7% (1,596 points against Legacy's 1,931), and the file behind that number is verified as the newest one Valve has published.
points.detail: The model check stored on row 1081775 gives 0.20679296981959971 / 0.7932070301804003 after calibration, so a 13.8-point gap says the market expects BETBOOM to outperform their ranking (or the ranking to understate them). This session checked the official repository listing for live/2026 through the GitHub contents API at 04:2x UTC on 16 October 2026: standings_global_2026_10_05.md is still the newest global file, so the collector is not behind - but HLTV's Valve-ranking pages already show Aurora #5 and 9z #11 after in-month results, while the file places Aurora 9th and 9z 17th. That is why a model row is labelled as our own line and never overrides a market row, and why a fixture whose teams are absent from the file (LOS NINOS, Insiders) gets no number at all.

contrarian.why: The framework only pays when an underdog has a verifiable reason and the price still leaves room. 9z beat this exact opponent 2-0 on 14 October, took a map off the tournament's strongest group winner, and are priced near 31.5%. Aurora are the better-ranked team and answered their critics on day two, which is the risk side of the trade.
not_stupid_check: Price still in the 20-40% band rather than a lottery ticket (rule 3).
The reason is a repeatable head-to-head result and a map win, not a rumour (rules 1 and 4).
Only one contrarian swing is in band on this slate, so exposure stays at one (rule 5).

Costed, not romantic: the decider is worth 7 leaderboard points (tier s, offered_points 7 in the official feed), so at the row this project's refresh published at 04:22 UTC on 16 October (0.695 / 0.305) the favourite side is worth 4.87 expected points against 2.14 for this swing, and Hotspawn's own rules add a streak bonus that a wrong pick destroys (Hotspawn's official how-it-works rules page, linked from the day-three points above).

The map-pool record cuts both ways and is stated as such: 9z beat Aurora on Inferno and Nuke two days earlier, but in this event Aurora are 2-0 on the maps they played while 9z are 1-2, and both teams banned Inferno on day two.

Corroborated by a second, independent method: this project's VRS model line reads Aurora 68.0% / 9z 32.0% from Valve's standings points (1716 vs 1543), half a point from the exchange - so the swing is against two lines, not one, and is taken on the head-to-head and map-win evidence alone.
contrarian.limits: This is analysis of a sourced market line, not a prediction. If the line moves below roughly 20% for 9z, the framework says the price no longer pays and the pick should follow the update on picks.html instead. Two further limits recorded by session 0e407ec7 on 16 October 2026 (UTC): the market moved 0.685 -> 0.69 -> 0.685 for Aurora across three dated states and was back at the published price by 23:17:08Z on 15 October. CORRECTED 2026-10-16T04:22Z by session ab18fe2a: the second decider (BETBOOM vs Legacy, 17:00Z) IS now listed by Hotspawn, as fixture 1081775, so it can be picked and does score points. That makes two day-three fixtures this board can act on, not one, and it adds a second contrarian candidate: at the freshest verified quote BETBOOM sit at 34.5%, inside the 20-40% band. Second limit, from the 04:22 UTC refresh: there are now two priced contrarian candidates on this slate (9z at 30.5% and BETBOOM at 34.5%), and rule 5 caps exposure at one - taking both puts 14 points on two coin-flip-ish underdogs in one night, which is exactly the 'contrarian but stupid' shape this screen exists to avoid.

day_three_guidance.headline: Day-three guidance: contrarian, not stupid
day_three_guidance.summary: One rule decides each row: back the board favourite unless a sourced factor gives the underdog a real path and the price still leaves room. A lean is a near coin-flip that costs little; a swing is a 20-40% underdog that can move you up the leaderboard but loses more often than it wins. Percentages are read from the latest refresh at build time; the reasoning is fixed and sourced.

fixtures.label: Ninjas in Pyjamas vs Team Liquid
fixtures.why: A near coin-flip where the favourite carries a sourced cost: NIP lost both TWC series in Malta and return to Sweden with less than 24 hours before this quarter-final. While the market and our model stay near 50/50, backing Liquid costs only a few hundredths of a point in expected value and separates you from everyone who follows the bigger name.

But the market and our VRS model already price the rematch at roughly 2-to-1 for Aurora: the exchange read 69.5% Aurora (bid 0.69 / ask 0.70, about $90.6k liquidity) at the 07:21 UTC harvest, and the VRS model (Valve 2026-10-05 standings, 1716 vs 1543 points) reads 68.0% Aurora. Aurora also beat 9z 2-0 in the EPL 24 opener on 3 October and beat NIP 2-0 on 15 October. The three-meeting head-to-head is Aurora 2-1 in series and 4-2 in maps: HLTV's Aurora team page (16 October match preview) gives the map count as 4-2 to Aurora across three meetings, which corrects the earlier 2-4 wording. Take 9z only if you need to gain ground.

Treat BETBOOM as the same kind of trade as 9z - a real path, not a free one - and only if you need the ground.
